newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soybean growers decline acreage forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soybean growers decline acreage forecast.

text.p: The president of the American Soybean Association declined to predict 1997/98 U.S. soybean acreage but said acreage above last year's 64.2 million acres would be "pretty significant."

At a press conference to kick off a meeting of corn and soybean producers, David Erickson predicted there would be expansion further west and that soybeans would take the place of some old program crops in the parts of the country.
"We think soybeans will fair pretty well," he said.
But he said there were artificial levels of soybeans acres last year due to the late spring planting.
"If you begin to see acreage reports much above last year that's a pretty significant increase. We've heard the number 65 million -- that's significant..." he said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department has projected 1997/98 soybean planted acreage at 65.3 million acres, the highest since the mid-1980's.
Erickson also said he did not think planting decisions would be all price driven, but that farmers would also be looking at crop rotation.
Last year's overhaul of U.S. farm policy removed almost all federal controls on what producers can grow.
ASA chairman John Long, a farmer in the southeast, said soybeans were "doing a better job than corn or cotton right now" in his region, adding, "we just have to see how the scenario plays out."
